# WrapYourGit

> WrapYourGit is an independent year in review for 2026, not affiliated with GitHub: it turns a developer's GitHub activity for one year into an animated, shareable story, a train ride through their contributions, streaks, busiest day, weekly rhythm, languages, top repositories, stars and forks, pull requests and reviews, developer archetype, a comparison with last year and a letter from Cell, the mascot. It is free and open source (MIT), works for any GitHub username, signs in with GitHub read-only, never reads source code, and every number on screen has a written definition.

Site: https://wrapyourgit.com. People also call this kind of recap "GitHub Wrapped", "wrap GitHub", "Git wrapped" or "GitHub year in review".

Any GitHub username has a recap of its public activity at https://wrapyourgit.com/<username>; signing in with GitHub adds private contribution counts to your own. Before 31 December the story says "so far" and can be synced again. Private repositories count toward totals but are never named in anything that can be shared.

## Pages

- [Home](https://wrapyourgit.com/): what the recap contains, the stations of the ride, the archetypes, what you can download, privacy facts and the FAQ
- [Privacy policy](https://wrapyourgit.com/privacy): what is read from GitHub, what is stored, what goes public and how to delete it

Recaps live at /<github-username>. Every username has one unless its owner hid it, so they are not listed here; each recap page is marked noindex.

## Details

- [Full description for language models](https://wrapyourgit.com/llms-full.txt): the stations, how the numbers are computed, downloads, privacy and the FAQ in one file
